page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / To show you the ropes
title: To show you the ropes
topic: Language for telling someone what to do
description:
Denise is back at Tip Top Trading and she's negotiated some new conditions with Paul. She's going to learn how to be a Sales Executive, which means Anna will need to help her with all the new tasks that go with this role. Will she be able to show Denise the ropes and teach her about being a top executive?
This episode focuses on the language that you might use when you are teaching a new colleague how to do your job.
phrases: Let me show you the ropes.
Watch what I do for a while.
Why don't you make a start on this?
I'm here to help, so please ask me if you need to know what to do.

listening_challenge.question: What task does Anna give Denise to do first?
listening_challenge.answer: Checking the database of clients to see who hasn't been called for a while.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Quick, gather round, here she comes.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Welcome back Denise, we just couldn't survive without you.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh bless you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes welcome back to Tip Top Trading Denise. Paul, the boss, was a little hasty in getting rid of her so now he's asked her back but negotiated some new conditions which include learning how to be a Sales Executive, like Anna. But who's going to show her what to do?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh, hello Denise. Nice to have you back. I suppose I had to eat my words didn't I?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes, well it makes a change from biscuits! Now, where have you put my stapler and my red pens?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Don't worry about that, I've got you a new stapler and a new desk, right here next to Anna.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh lovely.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well you wanted some experience in sales, so I thought Anna could show you the ropes.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Ropes? I don't have any ropes!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, if you 'show someone the ropes' it means you explain to someone how to do the job. You'll be great at that.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I see. Well I might know what to do but I'm no good at explaining it to someone else.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well the best way is to start at the beginning. Why not suggest to her to 'watch what I do', or give her some of your tasks and say 'please could you make a start on these?' and then reassure her by saying 'I'm here to help so please ask me if you need to know what to do.' Good luck.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thanks! So Denise, it's nice to have you back, how's your new desk?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Much bigger than my old one – and look, it goes up….and down.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes it does.  OK, shall we make a start then and I'll show you the ropes.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh yes Anna, of course Anna. Do I need to use the phone?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I reckon you're quite experienced with the phone already Denise!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Thank you Tom. We won't make any calls yet, just watch what I do for a while.  Look, I'm just checking our database so see who we haven't called for a while.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh yes.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm just checking the dates here…in fact Denise, why don't you make a start on this.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Of course…oh look, my phone's ringing.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Are you going to answer it then?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh right. Hello, Tip Top Trading, Denise speaking…oh hello Marge! (To Anna) It's Marge, Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. I'll leave you to it – I'm here to help, so please ask me if you need to know what to do.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: OK Anna, I won't be long. So Marge, how did it go the other night? Really? Really! Well, I'm sitting at my new desk…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Nice to have her back hey?! Some Sales Exec she's going to be!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Everyone has to start somewhere Tom! Now Anna is helping – or coaching - Denise I'm sure she'll become an excellent worker. Here are some of the phrases Anna used to help her:
Let me show you the ropes.
Watch what I do for a while.
Why don't you make a start on this?
I'm here to help, so please ask me if you need to know what to do.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Let's find out how Denise is getting on.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: So I said to him, it's just not my colour…yes exactly…hold on Marge, everyone's looking at me. I'd better call you back. Yes, tonight. Bye!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Hmm, you've certainly got a good phone manner. Do you think you could order some pens now, we've run out.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's not my responsibility anymore.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Err, I think it is.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Isn't!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Is.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Isn't!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: You two, please!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, she's got time for personal calls but not to order pens. Oh hold on….Oh Hi Jim, how's things? Yeah! Did you catch the match last night? What a goal!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear Anna. Things aren't going well. It's time to sort things out again but what are you going to do? Join us again next time to find out. Bye!
